# The Open Source Robotics Framework

Build, simulate, teleoperate, train, and deploy robots with one extensible Python framework—from hardware to AI control in one stack.

## Everything you need to build robots that learn

### Real-time control

Modules, kinematics, and an AI planner share one control loop, each running at the rate it needs.

#### Real-time modules

Solarian has a modular architecture: a robot is built from modules like an arm, a gripper, or a camera. Each runs in its own process at its own rate, so a 500 Hz arm never waits on a 30 Hz camera.

#### Kinematics built in

Command the end effector and the module solves inverse kinematics every tick, reporting the live pose through forward kinematics.

#### AI Agentic Controller

An agent harness around any vision-language model: give it a task in chat, and it plans the task and runs your physical skills as tools, each at its own rate.

### Simulate, plug in, reuse

Build a robot once, run it in MuJoCo or on hardware, and extend it with hardware and skill plugins.

#### Simulation built in

Declare a robot as a class with its modules as attributes. Set is_sim = True and the same modules and YAML drive a MuJoCo world instead of the hardware.

#### Plug-and-play hardware

Solarian is extended through plugins. Servo drivers, arms, grippers, and cameras install with solarian install , config included, and solarian create-plugin starts your own.

#### Plug-and-play skills

Skills install the same way: a motion plan, a scripted routine, or a learned policy that runs on any robot exposing the same actions.

### Learning policies

Go from teleoperated demonstrations to a trained policy driving the robot, without leaving the framework.

#### Session recording

solarian record keeps every camera as mp4 and every signal at its native rate, so no quality is lost.

#### Dataset management

Mirror, split, trim, and merge episodes into new versions without copying or losing data.

#### Policy training and serving

solarian train runs diffusion, ACT, or your own trainer, locally, on Modal, or on Solarian Base GPUs. solarian run-service then serves the policy to your skills.

### Developer utilities

The pieces every robotics project needs, built in.

#### Typed observations and actions

Pydantic schemas bound to your modules. What a sensor reads is what you stream, record, replay, and feed to a policy.

#### Hydra configuration

Every command reads composed YAML: robot.yaml , controller.yaml , one file per module. Override any value from the command line.

#### Calibration tools

solarian calibrate records joint limits and the home pose. Latency commands measure camera and actuator delay on your hardware.

## From idea to robot in three commands

Scaffold a project, attach a hardware module from a plugin, then run the relay server, the robot loop, and a controller — each on whatever machine makes sense.

# Scaffold a new project create-solarian myrobot cd myrobot # Install a plugin solarian install <plugin> # Run the three nodes solarian run-server solarian run-robot solarian run-controller

Built on a foundation of fast, production-grade tooling

### ZeroMQ

High-throughput PUSH/PULL and PUB/SUB sockets carry every action and observation between nodes.

### Hydra

Composable YAML configs for every command, every module, and every connection profile.

### PyTorch

First-class support for policies, vision-language models, and on-robot inference.

### Pydantic

Strong typing for configs, observations, actions, and inter-process messages.
